transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, I'm here because I've started catching myself thinking that... it would just be easier if I didn't wake up. And sometimes, like on the drive home from school, I start wondering if my family and my students would just be better off without me. It really scares me, because I don't want to act on it or anything. But the thoughts are there, so I figured I needed to come in and see someone.
How long have you been having these thoughts about not wanting to wake up or wondering if others would be better off without you?

It's been going on for a while now... I'd say about a year and seven months. It started right around the time I took over the STEM assessment redesign at school, which was just piled on top of my regular teaching load.
Have you noticed any changes in your ability to enjoy things you used to find pleasurable?

Yeah, definitely. I used to really look forward to things like playing softball, going to my book club, working in my garden... even the robotics club I help with at school. But now, I mostly just go through the motions if I actually show up. A lot of the time I just end up canceling, honestly, because none of it really feels enjoyable to me anymore.
Have you noticed any changes in your energy level or how quickly you're able to get things done?

Yes, my energy has definitely been a lot lower. It's like... by the time I get through a day of teaching and then a department meeting, my body just feels incredibly heavy. Getting anything else done after that, even just making dinner or trying to answer a few emails from parents, it just feels like climbing a steep hill. I just don't have the energy for it.
Have you been having any problems with your sleep?

Yeah, I have. It's actually really frustrating because I can be completely exhausted, but I'll still just lie awake in bed. My brain just keeps replaying all the assessment deadlines and... whatever classroom mistakes I made that day. And then when I finally do fall asleep, I usually wake up around 4 a.m., and I just never really get back to sleep after that.
Have you noticed any significant changes in your weight recently?

Yeah, I have. Um, I guess I've been losing weight. I'm not really trying to, but my clothes are definitely fitting a lot looser than they did a year ago. It's just... most school days, I either completely forget to eat or just avoid it until late in the afternoon. I just don't have much of an appetite.
Have you noticed yourself moving or speaking more slowly than usual, or the opposite, feeling restless and unable to sit still?

No, I haven't really noticed anything like that. Um... I don't think I'm talking or moving any slower than normal. And I'm not really restless or fidgety, either. I just feel exhausted, but physically, I think I'm moving around the same as I usually do.
Have you felt this way, with little interest or pleasure in things and feelings of worthlessness, for more than two years?

No, not quite two years. It's been going on for about a year and a half, maybe a year and seven months. It started right around the time I agreed to take over the STEM assessment redesign for the school, which was on top of my regular teaching load. That's when all of this really started to hit me.
Have you had periods like this before in your life, where you felt similarly, or is this the first time you've experienced these thoughts and feelings?

No, I haven't. Um... this is really the first time I've ever felt like this. I mean, I've had normal stress from teaching before, of course, but nothing like this. I've never experienced these kinds of feelings or thoughts until everything piled up a year and a half ago.
Have you been experiencing any feelings of anxiety or nervousness lately?

No, not really. I mean, I'm overwhelmed by the workload, but I wouldn't call it anxiety or nervousness. It's more just... this heavy feeling of being drained all the time, not like I'm on edge or panicking about things. Just tired.
Have you had any periods where your symptoms were significantly worse than they are now?

No, it's pretty much been a steady decline since it started. I wouldn't say there was a specific time where it was suddenly a lot worse... it's just been this constant, heavy feeling that hasn't really let up for the past year and a half.
Was there something specific that happened around the time you took over the STEM assessment redesign that you think might have triggered these feelings?

Not really, no. Um... there wasn't any big life event or anything like that, if that's what you mean. It was really just the redesign itself. Taking that on just added so much to my plate on top of my regular teaching schedule. So, no, nothing else specific happened around that time.

Would you say that these thoughts and feelings have been interfering with your ability to function at work or in your daily life most of the time, or is it more that they're just really unpleasant but you're still managing to get by?

I'd say it's definitely interfering most of the time. I wouldn't say I'm just managing to get by anymore. Um, I'm falling behind on my grading and lesson planning, and it's getting to the point where it's actually affecting my classroom. I even made a grading mistake recently that really scared me, because I used to be so meticulous about my work. 

And it's not just at school, either. I've basically stopped showing up for my friends and family the way I used to. It feels like my whole life has just narrowed down to barely getting through the school day, and then going home completely exhausted.
Have you experienced two months or more where you didn't have these feelings of worthlessness and lack of interest in activities?

No, I haven't. Since this all started about a year and a half ago, it's just been constant. There hasn't been a break at all, let alone a couple of months where I felt normal or interested in things again. It's just been this same heavy feeling the whole time.
Have you had these feelings of worthlessness and lack of interest in activities for most of every day?
Yeah, I would say so. Um... it really is most of the day. From the time I wake up for school until I finally go to bed, it doesn't really let up. It's just always there.
Do you think taking over the STEM assessment redesign was the main trigger for how you've been feeling?

Yeah, I really think it was. Um, this has all been going on for about a year and seven months now, which is exactly when it started—right after I took over the STEM assessment redesign on top of my regular teaching load. So, yes, I'd say that was definitely the trigger.
Have you had these feelings of worthlessness and lack of interest in activities for two years or more?

No, not quite two years. Like I just mentioned, it's been about a year and seven months. It all started right when I took over the STEM assessment redesign on top of my regular teaching load, so it hasn't reached the two-year mark yet.
Have you noticed any improvement in your symptoms at any point over the past year and seven months?
No, not really. I mean, I haven't noticed any time where I felt better or like things were getting back to normal. It's just been a steady feeling this whole time.
Do you think your symptoms will continue or have you started to feel like they might be improving now?

Honestly, I don't know if they'll continue. I haven't started to feel any different or... or like things are improving right now. It's just kind of been the exact same, so I really can't say if it's going to get better anytime soon.
